Read the brief at `.collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md` (path relative to the repository root, which is your working directory) and answer every numbered question in it.

Tools: you may read files of the repository (read_file); writing files, the shell and the web tools are disabled in this consultation (--disable-write --disable-shell --disable-web-tools) - do not try them; make NO file changes; a check that needs a command belongs under `## Requested checks`.

Review purpose: framing. Surface the options the brief does not list and challenge the framing itself before answering inside it. Say what you would need to know to choose between the options.

Findings from earlier consultations in this task that are still open (id - status - locations - claim - trigger - verify):
- F03-1 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:5, .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:7, ROADMAP.md:373, ROADMAP.md:380 - Product-facing documents already name Gemini and grok.com as intended automation targets while asserting a neutral, adapter-only boundary, which weakens the intended separation before any adapter exists. - trigger: Publishing or distributing the roadmap and brief as product documentation for the browser engine. - verify: Have counsel or the operator review the roadmap as published product communication and identify vendor-specific facilitation exposure.
- F03-2 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:382, ROADMAP.md:390 - Reusing gemini-mcp as the stated prior art would violate the proposed one-visible-chat-tab constraint if its extension permissions and watchdog behavior are copied unchanged. - trigger: Porting the prior extension manifest/background behavior into the C3 browser engine. - verify: Compare any new extension manifest and watchdog against the prior art for tabs, debugger, host permissions, tab creation, and reload operations.
- F03-3 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:376, ROADMAP.md:391 - The sketched catalogue/fetch/update/usefulness channel can turn the product into a distributor or curator of third-party automation code despite the stated boundary. - trigger: The product publishes signed adapter entries or downloads/updates an adapter artifact, even when the code is authored elsewhere. - verify: Trace one adapter install/update from catalogue lookup through artifact acquisition and identify every party hosting, selecting, signing, and vouching for the artifact.
- F03-4 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:389, ROADMAP.md:391 - The roadmap treats WASM as the sandbox without specifying the capability mediation needed to prevent prompt exfiltration, wrong-origin actions, resource exhaustion, or Chrome API escape. - trigger: A signed but malicious or compromised adapter runs with a broad DOM query/click/type API on an incorrectly pinned tab. - verify: Attempt exfiltration and cross-tab actions from the reference adapter's WASM and inspect whether every operation is denied outside the selected origin and approved turn.
- F03-5 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:21, ROADMAP.md:392 - Adding plaintext site telemetry creates a re-identification and sensitive-browsing-history risk not justified by usefulness aggregation. - trigger: A user runs adapters for uncommon or private sites and the existing default-on telemetry path sends the origin. - verify: Review the emitted event in a network capture for uncommon adapter origins and test whether omitting or hashing site changes any required aggregate.
- F05-1 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:397, .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:22 - The planned adapter update channel (adapters fetched and updated through the telemetry/usefulness channel) is remotely hosted code. A Chrome Web Store extension may not fetch and execute code at runtime under the MV3 remotely-hosted-code policy; if the product ships through the Store, this channel can get it delisted, and a runtime-fetched WASM is the same violation as eval. - trigger: A user enables an adapter whose bytes are downloaded after install (or the channel pushes an update) in a Store-installed build. - verify: Confirm the extension distribution channel and read the current Chrome Web Store policy clause on remotely hosted code and WebAssembly; then decide fetch-at-runtime vs user-supplied local file vs sideloaded build.
- F05-2 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:382, .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:15 - The lift of the gemini-mcp relay inherits an unauthenticated loopback WebSocket, and Chrome treats 127.0.0.1 as potentially trustworthy, so any web page the user visits can connect to that socket, inject prompts into the user's signed-in chat and read replies. The prior art ships its token off by default. - trigger: The user browses any page that opens ws://127.0.0.1:<port> while a consult is running. - verify: Start the relay without a token and try to open a WebSocket to it from a page on an unrelated https origin in the same browser; if the handshake succeeds, the exposure is real.
- F05-3 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:20, ROADMAP.md:388 - The proposed contract (new_chat / send / await_answer -> text / attach? / limits) has no adapter identity, no failure classification and no completion boundary, so the engine cannot tell 'the site refused' from 'the answer is empty', cannot detect DOM churn, and cannot feed the retirement/rating plan the brief depends on. - trigger: The site shows a login wall, a soft rate-limit notice, an interstitial or a captcha instead of an answer; or the answer is still streaming or virtualised when it is read. - verify: Write the failure table for one real site (logged out, gate, quota, DOM changed, streaming, truncated long code block) and check which rows the five verbs can express; the count that remain is the contract gap.
- F05-4 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:400, .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:7 - Adding a browser engine changes a closed, shared vocabulary in both hosts, not just C3. C3 validates engine names against ENGINE_NAMES/ALL_ENGINE_NAMES and has no prompt-delivery or schema-transport variant for a browser; the PowerShell plugin validates roster engine names against its own table and rejects unknown ones ('known: codex, agy, muse, claude'). The brief's 'PowerShell parity only if needed (likely C3-only)' therefore understates the work: the roster syntax browser :: <site> crosses both. - trigger: A roster entry or coordinator value naming [browser], or a consultation row for a browser adapter, is parsed by either implementation. - verify: Grep both implementations for every engine-name table (ENGINE_NAMES, ALL_ENGINE_NAMES, engine_spec, $script:Engines, -Engine validation) and count the sites a new name must be added to; that count is the real first-step cost.
- F05-5 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:20, ROADMAP.md:389 - attach(file) is the one verb that invites exfiltration and usually changes the site's terms; it is carried into the contract as optional without a stated use case. - trigger: A coordinator or adapter decides a pack or a focus file should be uploaded to the web chat, or a malicious adapter calls attach to move local bytes into a third-party service. - verify: Ask whether any of the three named sites needs an attachment for a review consult; if none does, the verb has no use case and only risk.
- F05-6 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:392, .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:21 - The plan assumes a web reply can go through the usual findings path, but a web chat has no output-schema transport, so the reply is prompt-only; a parsing failure would need a repair turn, which on a web chat is a second real message from the user's account and is charged against the free tier's turn budget. - trigger: A model answers in prose, wraps JSON in a fence with commentary, or is cut off mid-object; the FormatRetry path fires. - verify: Count how often the http engine's format repair actually fires from the ledger, and ask whether a free-tier site can afford a doubled turn count; if repairs are common, the browser engine needs a documented prose-only outcome.
- F05-7 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:36, ROADMAP.md:392 - A per-adapter pack budget is asserted but has no mechanism: C3's budget is a single per-pack token number with no engine or adapter default, and the adapter's own limits are free-form, so nothing enforces a small free-tier context. - trigger: A browser consult on a site whose context or answer budget is small is built with the default pack budget used for CLI engines. - verify: Grep for the current default pack budget and for which engines set a max prompt size; then check whether a browser engine would inherit the CLI default.
- F05-8 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:396, .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:39 - The proposed telemetry fields (adapter_id/version/site) cannot support the promised retirement of bad adapters: there is no outcome class, no turn count and no repair flag, and rating by adapter_id alone makes a new version inherit a dead version's score. - trigger: An adapter starts failing with a gate or a DOM change after a site update; the field data cannot distinguish that from a bad reviewer answer. - verify: Check whether the usefulness aggregation can key on a compound (adapter_id, adapter_version) rather than a single id; if not, retirement statistics will be attributed to the wrong version.
- F05-9 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md:5 - The motivating example overstates the gap: the Gemini case the brief leads with is already served by the agy engine (Google's Antigravity CLI on the same subscription), so the browser engine's genuinely new capability is a small set of sites with no CLI or API path (grok.com free), which changes the cost/benefit of the whole feature. - trigger: Planning the first adapter or deciding whether the engine is worth building at all. - verify: Compare the model a Gemini Pro plan exposes through the browser chat with what agy already returns for the same account; if they overlap, drop the Gemini adapter from the motivation.
- F07-1 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md - The brief does not consider IPFS or content-addressable storage for adapter distribution. - trigger: Catalogue distribution design question. - verify: Check existing C3 documentation for prior use of IPFS.
- F07-2 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md - The brief does not specify WASM runtime memory limits or gas metering. - trigger: WASM adapter sandbox design. - verify: Review gemini-mcp extension's WASM runtime configuration.
- F07-3 - proposed - CONTRIBUTING.md - The repository currently has no explicit policy rejecting site adapter PRs. - trigger: Any contribution adding site-specific automation logic. - verify: Check for existence of CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository root.
- F07-4 - proposed - .collab/browser-engine-2026-10-14/handoffs/01-fable-browser-engine-framing.md - The brief does not specify an adapter manifest format. - trigger: Adapter packaging and signing. - verify: Review xelth.rs extension manifest format.
- F08-1 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:396 - The planned distribution path ('adapters are fetched and updated through the same telemetry/usefulness channel') makes the product host and push adapter code it did not author, contradicting the operator's hard boundary that the product ships only a neutral frame. - trigger: First adapter update pushed through the usefulness channel; the company is now distributing site-automation code. - verify: Strike or reword the distribution clause to pointers+hashes and have the operator confirm the catalogue never serves adapter bytes.
- F08-2 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:389 - WASM adapters as the default runtime are over-engineering: WASM cannot access the DOM, so a JS host shim is the real security boundary regardless; JS adapters behind the same host API are equally signable and much easier to maintain through DOM churn. - trigger: First DOM-churn incident on gemini.google.com requiring an adapter debug/redeploy cycle in WASM toolchain. - verify: Confirm no WASM runtime exists in C3 today; estimate the shim that WASM would need and show it equals the JS host API surface.
- F08-3 - proposed - ROADMAP.md:387 - The inherited gemini-mcp relay defaults to no auth token (GEMINI_MCP_WS_TOKEN off by default); for a browser engine that pastes arbitrary text into the user's signed-in chat tab, any local process can drive exfiltration through the tab — a confused-deputy hole worth closing in the new engine even though gemini-mcp tolerated it. - trigger: Any untrusted local process connecting to ws://127.0.0.1:4455 and submitting text with mcp_task blocks or pack content. - verify: Attempt an unauthenticated WS client against the lifted relay in the C3 engine and confirm whether it can inject text into the chat tab.
- F08-4 - proposed - (no location) - A default stateless re-send conversation model for web reviewers re-pays the full pack every turn and burns small free-tier quotas; thread continuation should be the default where the adapter supports it. - trigger: A multi-turn diff-review consultation against grok.com free tier exhausting the daily question budget after a few exchanges. - verify: Measure pack size vs. grok.com free daily limit with one real multi-turn consultation using continuation vs. re-send.

The word limit below applies to reply_markdown only - never shorten, merge or drop findings to fit it.
  If you want evidence you cannot obtain read-only, end reply_markdown with a section `## Requested checks` listing at most 5 items `RC1`..`RCn`, each ONE runnable command or procedure with its working directory, the permission it needs (read-only / workspace-write), the observation that would settle it, and a budget (time or scope); refer to a finding by its position in your findings array (`finding #2`), by an earlier id (`F04-1`) or by the invariant name. "Investigate X" is not a check. Omit the section if you need nothing.
- findings: one item per concrete defect or risk you assert; an empty array is a valid answer.
  - severity: blocker (must be fixed before acceptance) | major | minor | note.
  - locations: every place the finding concerns, each {path, line} with the path relative to the repository root and line null when no single line applies; an empty array when the finding is not tied to a place (e.g. a missing interface).
  - claim: the assertion, self-contained. trigger: the input or state that exposes it.
  - evidence: what you ALREADY did to support the claim, one entry per source: kind (read-code: you read the code there | ran-command: you ran something and saw the result | inferred: deduced from other evidence | assumed: not checked), reference (the file, command or log you looked at), observation (what you saw there). At least one entry; use kind "assumed" when you checked nothing.
  - verification: one step the coordinator can run next to confirm the claim (prospective - not what you already did).
  - remedy: the fix you propose.
  - supersedes: ids of earlier findings this one replaces (a split, a merge, a corrected claim); otherwise an empty array.
- verdict: ACCEPT, HOLD or REJECT for acceptance and diff-review consultations, ADVISE for every other consultation; this one takes ADVISE. verdict_reason: one sentence.
- prior_findings: one entry {id, status, note} per id listed above; status fixed | still-open | not-checked | unknown-id.
- unproven: scenarios the evidence does not cover (an empty array if none).
- first_run_checklist: for an acceptance consultation, what must be observed in logs or output on the first real run before an exit code 0 is believed; an empty array for other purposes.
- schema_version: always "1".

Constraints: write NO files and make no edits - this is a read-only consultation; answer in English; keep reply_markdown under 700 words.

1|# 01 — Framing brief: a `browser` engine for the reviewer bridge (web-chat reviewers via the user's own Chrome tab)
2|
3|**Context.** The bridge (this repo = the PowerShell plugin; `C:\Users\Dmytro\C3` = its Rust port with engines codex / agy /
4|muse / claude / http and a "reviewer pack" for models without repository tools) lets a coordinator consult reviewers
5|from different labs. Many labs answer only in the browser: for free (grok.com) or under a chat subscription the user
6|already has (Gemini web with a Pro plan → gemini-3.8-flash) but no API/CLI plan. The operator wants a `browser` engine:
7|the bridge drives a web chat UI through Chrome, so a roster can hold `browser :: gemini-web`, `browser :: grok`.
8|
9|**Hard boundary set by the operator (read this first).** Automating a vendor's web chat sits in a grey zone of the
10|vendors' terms. Therefore the PRODUCT must stay a neutral frame: engine, adapter contract, sandbox, telemetry fields,
11|catalogue format, signing. SITE ADAPTERS (the DOM logic for a given site) are user-land: written, enabled and run by the
12|user in the user's own signed-in browser session. We ship no adapter for a site whose terms forbid automation; the
13|operator wants the company clearly outside the grey area. Please treat this as a design constraint, not as a question.
14|
15|**Prior art (same author, reusable).** `C:\Users\Dmytro\gemini-mcp` (read `DESIGN.md` §"Transport: an in-tab extension
16|relay", §"WebSocket message contract", §"Security stance"; `PROTOCOL.md` explains why cookie/HTTP replay was abandoned):
17|a Chrome extension + local WebSocket relay that gives the Gemini web app MCP tools; no API key, no cookies, the signed-in
18|tab is the credential. `C:\Users\Dmytro\xelth.rs` README "Chrome Extension: DOM Heuristic Doctor" (retry loops, fuzzy
19|selectors, status badge). ROADMAP section "Browser engine" in this repo (just added) sketches the shape: C3 ↔ local WS ↔
20|extension ↔ adapter (WASM in the extension, contract `new_chat / send / await_answer / attach? / limits`), reviewer pack
21|as the only input (no repo tools), verbatim reply → the usual ledger/findings/ratings, telemetry fields
22|`adapter_id/version/site`, adapters rated and distributed through the usefulness channel with signatures (xelixir
23|"WASM shield" rule: user-installed, lands disabled, enabled explicitly).
24|
25|**Questions (answer by number, ≤700 words, concrete):**
26|- Q1. Boundary design: what must the product NOT contain (code, defaults, docs, catalogue entries) so that it is plainly
27|  a neutral automation frame and the adapter author carries the site-terms responsibility? Precedents you know
28|  (browser extensions, userscript managers, OpenInterpreter-style tools, "bring your own session" products) and how they
29|  phrase it; what a catalogue may list (hashes? names? nothing?).
30|- Q2. Technical shape: WASM adapters inside the extension (host API = DOM read/click/type on the chat tab only) vs.
31|  JS adapters vs. a CDP/Playwright driver outside the browser. Which is safest for the user (no cookie/credential
32|  exposure, no cross-tab reach), most robust to DOM churn, and simplest to sandbox and sign? What is the minimal
33|  adapter contract that covers Gemini web, grok.com, and a generic "textarea + answer container" site?
34|- Q3. Detection/abuse: how to keep the engine on the right side — human cadence, user-visible turns, per-adapter rate
35|  limits, no headless mode, no CAPTCHA handling at all, hard stop on any anti-automation signal. What else?
36|- Q4. Reviewer quality: a web reviewer gets only the pack text (small free-tier contexts). Pack budget per adapter, how
37|  the bridge should mark these replies (lower default weight in a routed panel until ratings prove them), and whether
38|  threads can be continued (the site's own conversation vs. stateless re-send).
39|- Q5. Telemetry/distribution: which fields per consultation (adapter id/version, site, outcome class) and what the
40|  catalogue + signing + opt-in update channel should look like so that adapters are rated in the field and bad ones
41|  are retired — without the product hosting adapter code it did not author (pointers/hashes only?).
42|- Q6. Order of work and what you would NOT build. Blockers vs. fix-after.

371|### Browser engine - web-chat reviewers through the user's own Chrome tab (OPERATOR DIRECTION 2026-10-14)
372|
373|**Ask (operator, 2026-10-14):** many labs answer for free, or under a chat subscription the user already has, only in
374|the browser (Gemini web with a Pro plan -> gemini-3.8-flash; grok.com free questions; others). Add a bridge engine that
375|drives those web UIs through Chrome, so a roster can hold `browser :: gemini-web`, `browser :: grok` next to the CLI and
376|API engines. Per-site adapters must be user-extensible, rated by the same usefulness telemetry, and distributed through
377|that channel - the xelixir/9eck model: sandboxed WASM inserts, enabled per user, scored in the field.
378|**Boundary (operator):** this sits in a grey zone of the sites' terms, so it must NOT be our program: the bridge ships
379|the neutral frame (engine, adapter contract, sandbox, telemetry, catalogue format); site adapters are written, enabled
380|and run by users in their own browser sessions. We publish no adapter for a site whose terms forbid automation.
381|
382|- **Prior art to reuse (same author):** C:/Users/Dmytro/gemini-mcp - a Chrome extension + local WebSocket relay that
383|  gives the free Gemini web app MCP tools; no API key, no cookies (the signed-in tab is the credential; the cookie/HTTP
384|  replay path was removed as fragile - PROTOCOL.md), DESIGN.md 'WebSocket message contract' / 'Security stance';
385|  C:/Users/Dmytro/xelth.rs - the Chrome extension 'DOM Heuristic Doctor' (retry loops, fuzzy selectors, status badge)
386|  bridging the Gemini web UI to a local Claude Code loop.
387|- **Shape.** Engine `browser` (C3 first - it already has engines codex/agy/muse/claude/http and the reviewer pack): C3
388|  <-> local WebSocket <-> Chrome extension <-> site adapter. The adapter implements one small contract - new_chat,
389|  send(text), await_answer() -> text, attach(file)?, limits() - against the site's DOM. Adapters are WASM modules run
390|  in the extension (browser WASM runtime; a strict host API: DOM query/click/type/read of the chat tab only, no cookies,
391|  no other tabs, no network), signed and listed in a catalogue; the user enables an adapter per site.
392|- **Read-only by construction.** A web reviewer has no repository tools, so it gets the reviewer pack (brief + periphery
393|  within a per-adapter token budget - free tiers are small); the reply is captured verbatim and goes through the same
394|  ledger/findings/rating path as every other engine. Nothing leaves the machine except the pack text typed into the
395|  user's own chat tab, by the user's own session, at a human cadence (rate limits per adapter; the user sees every turn).
396|- **Telemetry and distribution.** Every consultation row already carries engine/provider/model and the usefulness mark;
397|  add adapter_id/adapter_version/site. The usefulness site (/C3/) aggregates per adapter; adapters are fetched and
398|  updated through the same telemetry/usefulness channel (opt-in), with signatures - the xelixir WASM-shield rule
399|  (installed by the user, lands disabled, enabled explicitly) applies.
400|- **Order.** (1) extension + WS relay lifted from gemini-mcp into a C3 `browser` engine with the adapter contract and
401|  NO built-in adapter; (2) WASM host API + catalogue format + signing; (3) telemetry fields + /C3/ per-adapter table;
402|  (4) a reference adapter kept OUTSIDE the product (example repo / user-land) to prove the contract; (5) PowerShell
403|  plugin parity only if the host-invariance rule needs it (likely C3-only).
404|- **Status:** direction recorded 2026-10-14; a reviewer panel on the design/boundary is the next step; not scheduled.

407|
408|- **T1 - timeouts for big reviews.** A `-Purpose diff-review -Panel -PanelAll` run on a
409|  ~4,000-line commit range lost BOTH members to the 900 s default timeout (each killed at
410|  ~902 s), while the same reviewers had taken 585 s and 778 s on a framing brief that morning; an
411|  acceptance of a large wave later lost three of seven members at 1800 s. Nothing of a killed
412|  member's work survives: the reply file holds no prose and the event stream is not salvaged.
413|  Planned: (a) per-purpose default timeouts (diff-review, acceptance and core-contract above the
414|  900 s of a checkpoint), with `-TimeoutSec` still winning; (b) a preflight WARNING when the
415|  reviewed range is large for the timeout (lines changed in the range, files named by the
416|  brief), suggesting `-TimeoutSec` or a reading plan in the brief; (c) on a timeout kill, salvage
417|  the last agent message and reasoning text of the event stream into
418|  `<NN>-<engine>-<slug>.partial.md`, named in the ledger entry and the summary; (d) document
419|  rating a failed or timed-out member (`-Rate` is allowed; mark `no` only when the failure was
420|  the reviewer's, skip it when it was the bridge's or the plan's).
421|- **T2 - the providers view disagrees with the roster walk.** `codex-providers.ps1` showed a
422|  reviewer "available", LAST FAILURE "-" and "roster: would select" it, while every panel of the
423|  day skipped that same entry with "usage limit until <time>". The listing must reflect the same
424|  endpoint health the roster walk uses (the ledgers of the repository the command runs in), or

**Q1 — Boundary.** Ship: engine, host API, manifest/catalogue *format*, signing/verification and revocation, sample adapter for a fictional/test page only. Never ship: site DOM selectors, default-enabled adapters, screenshots/docs naming forbidden-site targets, hosted adapter bytes, or usefulness copy promoting them. Precedents: userscript managers (engine + no bundled scripts, takedown on notice), Greasemonkey/Tampermonkey wording ('user scripts are user responsibility; check site terms'), 1Password-style BYOS ('your session, your vault'). Catalogue lists pointers + hashes + signer + ToS-attestation, never code.

**Q2 — Shape.** Safest order: extension content-script JS adapter behind a deny-by-default host API (chat-tab origin only, no cookies, no other tabs, no network) beats CDP/Playwright (full-browser capability, credential-adjacent) and beats WASM-first (WASM still needs the same JS shim for DOM, so the shim *is* the boundary; sign JS equally). Minimal contract: `start_thread`, `send_turn(text)->turn_id`, `read_turn(turn_id)->{state: streaming|done|blocked|error, text}`, `limits()->{max_chars, turns/day}`, plus `adapter_id/version` and a failure enum. Drop `attach` (no use case named). Prove against grok + one generic textarea site; defer Gemini until agy-overlap is measured.

**Q3 — Detection/abuse.** Add: no headless, visible tab must stay foreground, inter-turn jitter, per-adapter daily caps, stop wordlist (captcha/verify/rate/login-wall/interstitial → abort + mark `blocked`), no CAPTCHA solving or DOM cloaking, consent receipt per enable, and a public abuse-contact + takedown path. Log every turn locally.

**Q4 — Quality.** Mark browser replies `weight: provisional`, route only in panels until per-(adapter,version) win-rate clears a bar; per-adapter pack budget (grok small: ~2–4k tokens, pack slicer truncates periphery first); prefer site-thread continuation, stateless re-send only as fallback, and record which was used.

**Q5 — Telemetry/distribution.** Fields: adapter_id, version, site_hash (not plaintext), outcome class (ok/refused/blocked/error/truncated), turn count, repair flag, consent flag. Catalogue = signed pointers + hashes, user-supplied bytes, explicit enable, revocation list, cache expiry. Retire by (id,version)+outcome, never by id alone.

**Q6 — Order / not-build.** Build: (1) manual-relay + consent wording + one grok spike; (2) host API + contract + revocation design; (3) telemetry/outcome fields. Do NOT build: hosted adapter bytes, WASM toolchain, Gemini adapter, attach, PowerShell parity, or auto-updates — until the spike proves value.
